_readme: All resume text lives here. Edit this file and push to GitHub; the live site updates automatically. The page shows each job's 'key' bullets (3 is best) and hides 'creative', 'highlights', and 'earlier_roles' behind a 'More' link. Work items with "featured": true show first; the rest appear under 'See all work'. The 'intro' block sets the welcome pop-up's text, choices, and delay; answers are saved to the visitor_intros table in Supabase. A job's optional 'since' note (for example 'At Fromm since 2005') shows under its dates. A certificate's 'status' (for example "Completed" or "In progress, Fall 2026") shows next to it; anything not completed is left out of the data Google reads. The page shows the short versions: each job's 'line' and 'points' (2-3 bullets, 12 words or fewer), each work item's 'caption' and 'tag', 'skills_short', and 'partners'. The longer 'summary', 'key', 'areas', 'tags', and full 'skills' sit behind 'More' and are used for the printed resume.
_work_help: Each item in 'work' is one card. Optional: 'image' (or 'images': a list of {"src", "alt"} for a small gallery) (a picture you put in public/work/, e.g. "/work/poster.jpg"), 'imageFit': "contain" or "contain-light" (show a logo or screenshot whole on a dark or white background instead of cropping it), 'video' (a YouTube or Vimeo link; YouTube also gives the card its picture), 'link' (any web page), 'role', 'collaborators', 'details'. 'category' is one name, or a list of names, from: Web design, Product design, Project design, Print design, Video, Storytelling, Marketing, Events, Collaborations, Technology, AI. Featured pieces can also be case studies: add 'challenge', 'approach', and 'outcome' (with 'role' as your part); the open view then shows them as sections.
name: Herbert Gracia
tagline: I build brands, then the businesses behind them.
about: My strength is connecting brand strategy, creative thinking, and marketing with execution, from concept and product development through campaign, production, digital platforms, sales, and customer experience.

My background spans brand strategy, creative direction, art direction, integrated marketing, visual storytelling, video, product development, manufacturing, sales, technology, AI, and experiential marketing. I also use AI and generative AI in campaign development, content creation, audience messaging, research, social media marketing, and creative workflows.

work.title: State of Flux
work.summary: Building a brand from the ground up: identity, apparel, retail, e-commerce, and co-branded collaborations.
work.role: Co-Founder & Brand Director: brand strategy, identity, creative direction, product, and marketing, leading a team of 5

images.alt: Three State of Flux trucker caps in green, white, and black, each with an embroidered orange tiger
A pile of black and gold State of Flux woven labels reading 'Workshop Product'
A model outside a storefront wearing a black and orange Timbuk2 × State of Flux crossbody bag

work.challenge: Launch a new apparel brand in a crowded market and give people a reason to notice it, while I kept my full-time role at Fromm.
work.approach: I built a clear identity and product language, from embroidered tiger caps to woven 'Workshop Product' labels. Then I grew reach through co-branded products, events, and pop-ups with Pinterest, Timbuk2, and SFMOMA, and sold direct to customers and to companies through our store, e-commerce, wholesale, and B2B.
work.outcome: An independent brand with its own retail store, online shop, and co-branded collections with three well-known partners. In 2024 I exited by selling my ownership stake to my business partner.
work.caption: An apparel brand built from zero: identity, product, retail, e-commerce.

work.title: FAZE Apparel
work.summary: From concept to full acquisition: brand, apparel collections, wholesale distribution, trade shows, and our own retail store.
work.role: Co-Founder & Brand Director, leading a team of 5 across design, product, marketing, and sales
work.imageAlt: The FAZE Apparel storefront on a San Francisco street corner, with the FAZE lightning-bolt banner
work.challenge: Turn a new apparel label into a real business: products people wanted, stores willing to carry them, and a brand strong enough to attract a buyer.
work.approach: I led the identity, apparel graphics, lookbooks, photography, and seasonal campaigns, and ran product development from sampling and sourcing to manufacturing and quality control. I designed our trade-show booths in Las Vegas, Miami, Los Angeles, and New York, and designed and built our own retail store.
work.outcome: Grew to 10+ retail locations plus our own store, then sold the entire business in 2019 to a privately held company, including all intellectual property, trademarks, logos, designs, and brand assets.
work.caption: Concept to full acquisition: collections, trade shows, 10+ retail locations.

work.role: Designed the 50th Anniversary logo; leading brand, marketing, and PR for the celebration
work.imageAlt: Fromm Institute 50th anniversary graphic: a purple and gold '50, 1976–2026' badge over a collage of photos of members through the years
work.challenge: Mark 50 years (1976–2026) in a way that honors the Institute's history and brings in new members and supporters.
work.approach: I designed a bold purple-and-gold '50' badge, paired it with archival photos of members across five decades, and carried it across events, print, digital, and press.
work.caption: The anniversary logo I designed, carried across events, print, and press.

work.title: Frommcast
work.summary: Bringing a digital learning product to life: platform, video production, branding, and distribution.
work.role: Built the platform; lead its video and content
work.imageAlt: The Fromm Institute YouTube channel with the 'Learn Anytime, Anywhere with Frommcast!' banner and recorded lecture thumbnails
work.challenge: Give older adults a way to keep learning from home, beyond the classroom.
work.approach: I built the recording and hybrid-classroom setup, produced the lecture video, and launched it as Frommcast, a branded channel organized by subject on YouTube.
work.outcome: 200+ recorded classes on art, history, science, and more, free for anyone to watch. The YouTube channel I launched reached 700+ subscribers in its first 6 months.
work.caption: 200+ recorded classes; 700+ YouTube subscribers in six months.

work.imageAlt: The Fromm Institute for Lifelong Learning at the University of San Francisco logo in gold on black
work.challenge: Fromm started with no marketing presence, which limited how many new older learners it could reach.
work.approach: I built an integrated program across web, email, print, social, video, and paid digital on Google, Meta, and LinkedIn, and partnered with retirement communities, donor networks, and city agencies to reach new learners.
work.outcome: Because of this marketing, enrollment grew 10%. Fromm now serves about 1,000 students a session and 3,000 a year.
work.caption: Integrated campaigns across web, email, print, social, video, and paid.
